content: Classically, bag-of-words (Bow) methods were used to obtain representations of the documents in a corpus in terms of vectors of term frequencies weighted by inverse document frequency (TF-iDF). While such methods provide a statistical description of documents, they do not carry information about the order or proximity of words to each other since they regard word tokens in an independent manner with no semantic or syntactic relationships considered. Furthermore, BoW representations tend to be high-dimensional and sparse, due to large sizes of word dictionaries and low frequencies of many terms.
